summary: Iteration 5 frontend-only validation of ARIS-9 'escuta sempre' + wake word (server started via `cd /app && python3 server.py`, tested at http://localhost:8000 as Nyx, mobile 390x844, 3 Playwright runs, zero page/console errors). ALL 12 requested checks PASS. (1) APIs: typeof window.aris9Voice.startContinuousRecord === 'function' and typeof window.aris9Voice.createWakeWordDetector === 'function'; aris9Prefs.get() contains voiceAlwaysListen=false, wakeWordEnabled=false, wakeWord='aris' by default. (2) PERSISTENCE: set(voiceAlwaysListen=true), set(wakeWordEnabled=true), set(wakeWord='computador') -> written to localStorage 'aris9_agent_prefs' and all three survive a full page reload. (3) DRAWER: [data-testid=mode-always] and [data-testid=mode-wake] exist exactly once, both inside [data-testid=drawer-modes]; checking them sets aris9Prefs.voiceAlwaysListen/wakeWordEnabled to true. (4) SYNC drawer->voice mode: after checking both in the drawer, ESC to close, window.openVoiceChat() -> overlay has .open, [data-testid=vc-always-listen] CHECKED, [data-testid=vc-wake-toggle] CHECKED, vc-wake-word='aris'. Reverse sync also verified (toggling vc-always-listen then reopening drawer shows mode-always checked). (5) HEADER: vc-always-listen, vc-wake-toggle, vc-wake-word (default 'aris'), vc-voice-select (exactly 9 options), voice-chat-close, voice-mic-btn, voice-stop-btn all present and visible. (6) WAKE ACTIVATION: checking vc-wake-toggle sets #vc-status to 'Wake word ativa: diga "aris" para começar.' and pref wakeWordEnabled=true. (7) WORD CHANGE: filling vc-wake-word='computador' + change event -> pref wakeWord='computador' and detector reboots (status becomes 'Wake word ativa: diga "computador" para começar.'). (8) DEFENSIVE (SpeechRecognition removed from window): no crash, status = 'Wake word indisponível: Reconhecimento de fala local não suportado neste navegador (use Chrome/Edge).', checkbox auto-unchecked, pref reverted to false. (9) VAD: startContinuousRecord({silenceMs,maxMs,minMs,threshold,onLevel}) accepted the full option signature and resolved cleanly (Playwright fake mic produced audio; Whisper returned a transcript); isRecording()===false afterwards so no mediaStream/recorder left open. createWakeWordDetector('teste', cb) returns {start,stop,isActive} functions with isActive()===false before start. (10) REGRESSION voice mode: overlay opens with .open, mic/stop/close testids present, ✕ removes .open. (11) REGRESSION backend POST /api/voice/tts: 200 audio/mpeg 6912 bytes for {text:'oi',voice:'nova'}; invalid voice -> 400 JSON with readable pt-BR message (improved vs iteration 4 which returned 500). (12) REGRESSION drawer mobile: hamburger sets aria-expanded=true and moves focus to drawer-btn-terminal, ESC sets aria-expanded=false and restores focus to mobile-menu-btn. No real audio recording or real speech recognition was exercised, per request.
critical_code_review_comments: js/voice.js createWakeWordDetector returns a no-op setWord(w) stub (empty body). Either implement it (stop()+_boot() with the new word) or remove it from the public object — a silently no-op method is a trap for future callers.

js/voice.js startContinuousRecord has no cancel/abort handle: if the user closes the voice overlay while VAD recording is in flight, the requestAnimationFrame loop and AudioContext keep running until silence/maxMs and the already-resolved transcript still flows into _handleTranscribedText (agentSend + TTS run for a closed overlay). Consider returning an abort() or checking an epoch/token before the agent turn.

js/voice.js fallback path when AudioContext is unavailable resolves after a fixed 4000ms but never invokes onLevel and ignores minMs/maxMs — acceptable, but document it or reuse maxMs instead of the magic 4000.

js/voice-chat.js _startTalking non-VAD branch never sets busy=true (only the VAD branch does), so a rapid second mousedown can call startRecord() twice; startRecord/stopRecord tolerate it today but the guard is asymmetric.

js/voice-chat.js is 300 lines and fine, but the global document keydown handler registered in _build stays attached after close() — it early-returns on !overlay.classList.contains('open'), so no bug, just noted.
seed_data_creation: None. Prefs mutated during test were reset to defaults (voiceAlwaysListen=false, wakeWordEnabled=false, wakeWord='aris') at the end of each run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Server is NOT auto-started by supervisor here; run `cd /app && nohup python3 server.py &` and test at http://localhost:8000. Login: #auth-username/#auth-password/#auth-form submit; note #auth-overlay is hidden via the [hidden] attribute, so wait with page.wait_for_function("document.getElementById('auth-overlay').hidden === true") — wait_for_selector('#auth-overlay[hidden]') times out because the element is not visible. Playwright Chromium DOES expose webkitSpeechRecognition and a fake mic device, so wake word activates for real and getUserMedia succeeds (startContinuousRecord actually calls Whisper). To exercise the defensive branch, set window.SpeechRecognition=undefined; window.webkitSpeechRecognition=undefined before toggling vc-wake-toggle, and use page.click (not page.check) since the app reverts the checkbox. Real audio/voice recognition flows (auto follow-up after TTS, _pulseMic glow) were intentionally not exercised.
rca_of_the_issue: No defects found in the iteration 5 feature set. The two Playwright failures seen mid-run were test-harness artifacts, not app bugs: (a) wait_for_selector('#auth-overlay[hidden]') waits for visibility of an already-hidden node; (b) page.check() on vc-wake-toggle fails by design because the app's defensive handler unchecks it when SpeechRecognition is missing — replaced with page.click() + state assertions.
